rows.note: This is the everyday noun phrase for one swimming session or a swim; Cantonese otherwise commonly expresses the idea with a verb phrase.

example.english: I want to go for a swim today.
example.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 jat6 soeng2 heoi3 jat1 ci3 jau4 seoi2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for moving through water, including swimming a distance or doing laps.

example.english: We swim ten lengths every morning.
example.traditional: 我哋朝朝游水游十個塘。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 ziu1 ziu1 jau4 seoi2 jau4 sap6 go3 tong4

rows.note: Use this when someone feels dizzy or has a spinning sensation.

example.english: I swim until I feel dizzy, so I have to get out and rest.
example.traditional: 我游水游到頭暈，唯有上水休息。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jau4 seoi2 jau4 dou3 tau4 wan4 wai4 jau5 soeng5 seoi2 jau1 sik1

rows.note: Use this construction when saying that someone has a large quantity of something, such as money.

example.english: They have lots of money, so they swim every day without having to scrimp.
example.traditional: 佢有好多錢，日日游水都唔使慳。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jau5 hou2 do1 cin2 jat6 jat6 jau4 seoi2 dou1 m4 sai2 haan1

rows.note: Use this when a place or object is flooded or drenched with water.

example.english: The heavy rain flooded the whole street, so we can't swim today.
example.traditional: 場大雨搞到成條街水浸，今日冇得游水。
example.jyutping: coeng4 daai6 jyu5 gaau2 dou3 seng4 tiu4 gaai1 seoi2 zam3 gam1 jat6 mou5 dak1 jau4 seoi2
